title: Game engine: port pypan.py to TypeScript
description: Port the Python/curses game (etc/pypan.py, documented in SPEC.md) to a pure TypeScript engine in src/engine with no DOM dependencies. Faithful port first: preserve existing behavior and quirks; fixes and additions are tracked under the 'Gameplay fixes & additions' epic.
design:
Agreed architecture:
- Generator functions: game flows are function* that yield prompts and receive the player's answer, mirroring the Python's blocking display.say/ask_* calls line for line.
- Prompt protocol: a small closed union: say (optional art), yn, choose (labeled options, cancellable), number (with max, for 'All').
- Game driver: wraps the generator; exposes prompt and answer(value).
- RNG: one seedable PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) injected into the engine; never Math.random. Helpers mirror Python: chanceOf, randrange, inRange, randfloat.
- Saving: checkpoint saves of Hong state (same JSON shape as pypan.json) at the top of the port menu, as the Python does.

title: Engine: bank and interest
description: Port visit_bank (deposit/withdraw, Hong Kong only) and per-voyage interest (BANK_RATE 5%, LOAN_RATE 10%). SPEC.md section 4.4.

title: Engine: Elder Brother Wu (lender)
description: Port visit_wu (emergency bailout with escalating bailout multiplier, warning when cashless, repay up to min(cash,debt), borrow up to 2*cash-debt) and check_lender (threat above DEBT_THREAT_LEVEL, offer to visit, 1-in-4 robbery after month 12). Expose a reusable 'Wu covers the shortfall' helper for repairs and extortion. SPEC.md section 4.5.

title: Engine: warehouse, transfers and lorcha
description: Port check_warehouse (free transfers at home; lorcha 1-in-6 away after month 12 at 5-9% fee; otherwise transfer=-1; warehouse upgrade 1-in-10 at home after month 12) and transfer (fee skims arriving quantity). SPEC.md section 10.

title: Engine: shipyard (repairs, new ship, guns)
description: Port check_upgrades: offer_repair (McHenry, partial repairs, Wu covers shortfall), offer_ship (+50 capacity, clears damage), offer_gun (gun takes 10 units). SPEC.md section 9.

title: Engine: special cargo consignments
description: Port check_cargo / random_cargo: delivery payout on arrival at destination; 1-in-20 offers from month 18; size 5-30% of ship; one at a time. SPEC.md section 12.

title: Engine: hazards (police, muggers, warehouse fire)
description: Port check_safety: opium confiscation + fine, mugging above ROBBERY_CASH_LIMIT, warehouse fire. SPEC.md section 11.

title: Engine: Li Yuen extortion
description: Port check_extortion: counter cycle, summons when away, demand sizes early vs after month 12, refusal warning, Wu covers the shortfall. SPEC.md section 8.

title: Engine: storms
description: Port check_storm: 1-in-10; damage / blown off course / safe passage; returns possibly changed destination. SPEC.md section 6.

title: Engine: pirate battles
description: Port PirateBattle (pirate fleet only, as wired today): setup (count, health, damage factor, booty), player turn (fire/dump/run with run_ik/run_ok ratchet and partial escapes), enemy turn (gun hits vs hull damage), resolution. Keep PIRATE_KING plumbing (id multiplier) for later. SPEC.md section 7.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario tests: win by firing (booty added), flee, partial escape, gun destroyed frees 10 capacity. The dump_cargo min(1,...) quirk is ported as-is with a test documenting it.

title: Engine: voyage, comprador loop, new game / restore
description: Port sail_away (overload check, destination choice, advance time, pirates, storm, interest, arrival sequence in SPEC.md 5.1 order), establish_opts, compradors_loop, save_and_exit, and the startup choice (guns / debt / restore). Emit a checkpoint event at the top of each port-menu iteration for the UI to save.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end scenario: start, buy, sail, arrive, sell, exit, all with a fixed seed and scripted answers.

title: Scaffold TypeScript project
description: Move Python to etc/, add Vite + TypeScript + Vitest + fast-check + jsdom, README, smoke test.

title: Engine: property/fuzz tests for whole-game invariants
description: fast-check: random answer sequences across many seeds for thousands of steps. Invariants: no exceptions; cash, debt, bank, goods never negative; warehouse within capacity; save round-trips at every checkpoint. Record any ported quirks that violate an invariant as issues under the fixes epic rather than fixing them here.

title: Storage: SaveStore interface + localStorage implementation
description: src/storage: async SaveStore interface (load/save/clear/has), LocalStorageStore with try/catch around every access. Optional import of a pypan.json from the Python version. The interface is the seam for Cloudflare cloud saves later.

title: UI: green-screen terminal shell
description: index.html + src/ui/styles.css + terminal.ts: green-on-black styling, self-hosted monospace font with fallback, glow, optional scanlines (respect prefers-reduced-motion), message pane with dated header, ASCII art blocks (BOAT, STORM, PIRATES) in pre, skippable typewriter effect replacing SLEEP_LEVEL.

title: UI: touch input widgets for each prompt type
description: say: tap anywhere / Continue bar. yn: big Y/N buttons. choose: numbered button list, Cancel when cancellable. number: custom on-screen keypad (0-9, backspace, ALL, OK) so the iOS keyboard never appears. Hardware keyboard on iPad: digits, option first letter, Y/N, A for all, Enter, Esc. Tap targets at least 44px.
acceptance_criteria: jsdom tests: keypad clamps to max, ALL fills max, Esc/Cancel only when allowed, keyboard and touch produce identical answers.

title: UI: status, warehouse and hold panes + responsive layout
description: Status (location, date, cash, debt, bank, guns, repair %), Canton Warehouse, Ship's Hold (incl. special cargo). CSS grid: iPad landscape = curses layout; portrait / iPhone = compact status strip + collapsible hold/warehouse, message pane, bottom input dock.

title: UI: start screen and game wiring
description: main.ts: start screen (Guns / Debt / Restore when a save exists), drive the Game, re-render panes after each step, save on every checkpoint event, exit returns to start screen.
acceptance_criteria: A full game is playable in desktop Safari/Chrome and survives a reload by resuming from the last checkpoint.

title: UI: iOS polish and Add to Home Screen
description: 100dvh, env(safe-area-inset-*) padding, touch-action: manipulation, -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%, no rubber-band scroll of the shell, apple-mobile-web-app-capable + web manifest + icons for standalone mode, theme-color black.

title: UI: test on iPhone and iPad
description: iOS Simulator Safari (iPhone small + large, iPad portrait + landscape, iPad with hardware keyboard) and a real device via vite --host. File issues for anything found.

title: dump_cargo improves escape odds by at most 1 (min vs max)
description: PirateBattle.dump_cargo does run_ok += min(1, int(n/10)), so dumping any amount helps by at most 1. SPEC says escape odds grow with the amount dumped; probably meant max or no cap.

title: Storm damage threshold uses absolute damage, not percent
description: check_storm checks ship_damage < 80 (raw units) while is_gun_hit uses damage as a percent of ship size. Decide on one meaning.

title: Green-screen web UI for iPad and iPhone
description: Green-screen terminal-style HTML UI (src/ui) over the engine's Game API, optimized for touch on iOS Safari (iPhone + iPad), with hardware-keyboard support on iPad.
design: Vanilla TS + CSS, no framework. Black background, phosphor-green monospace, subtle glow, optional scanlines (off under prefers-reduced-motion). Self-hosted font with system monospace fallback. iPad landscape mirrors the curses layout (message pane left; Status / Canton Warehouse / Ship's Hold right). Portrait/iPhone: compact status strip, message pane, input dock at bottom.

title: Ship can sink / game over
description: Hull damage can exceed 100% with no consequence. Add sinking (and a game-over flow) when damage reaches the ship's capacity.

title: Win / retirement condition
description: No win condition exists. Add retirement (e.g. at a net-worth threshold, like the original Taipan!'s millionaire ending) with a final score screen.

title: Li Yuen's pirate fleet battles
description: PIRATE_KING is defined but never triggered. Wire Li Yuen encounters into voyages, influenced by whether extortion has been paid. SPEC.md section 16.

title: Jade event
description:
Source TODO: 'Make jade an event'.

From features.txt: right now jade is available as a good for purchase right out of the gate. Consider hiding it at first, and then having some kind of event that would introduce it into the world. What could the event be? What would trigger it? Would it require some kind of investment?

title: Resume mid-event via seed + answer-log replay
description: Checkpoint saves lose in-progress events (e.g. a battle) on reload, which lets players dodge pirates by reloading. Persist the RNG seed and the answers given since the last checkpoint, and replay them on load to restore the exact prompt.

title: Deploy static build with Cloudflare Workers Static Assets
description: wrangler config serving dist/; deploy script; custom domain optional.

title: Cloud saves via Worker + KV or D1
description: Small Worker API keyed by an anonymous player id; a RemoteSaveStore implementing SaveStore, falling back to localStorage when offline.

title: randomOtherCity never picks Batavia
description: NUM_CITIES is len(CITIES)-1 = 6 and random_other_city uses randrange(NUM_CITIES), so Batavia (6) is never chosen for storm diversions or cargo destinations. Ported faithfully; test in test/engine/constants.test.ts documents it.

title: in_range(lo, hi) returns lo..hi-2
description: in_range is lo + randrange(hi - 1 - lo), so in_range(5, 31) gives prices 5-29 (SPEC says 5-30), and every other in_range call is similarly short by two at the top. Ported faithfully; test in test/engine/rng.test.ts documents it. Fixing changes many ranges at once, so check each call site.

title: Bailout multiplier is never increased
description: SPEC says the bailout multiplier makes each successive emergency loan more expensive, but pypan.py only initializes it to 1 and reads it in visit_wu; nothing increments it. Ported faithfully; test 'never raises the bailout multiplier' in test/engine/lender.test.ts documents it.

title: Gameplay fixes & additions (post-port)
description: Behavior changes deliberately deferred until after the faithful port: quirks found in the Python, and TODOs from SPEC.md section 16. Each is a small, separate change whose test flips from documenting the old behavior to asserting the new.

title: Wu's robbery only happens if he has NOT threatened you
description: check_lender robs you of all your cash (after month 12, 1-in-4) only when 'not hong.threatened'. SPEC frames the robbery as a consequence of ignoring the debt, so it should likely require that Wu HAS threatened you (and perhaps that debt is still above DEBT_THREAT_LEVEL). As written, a small debtor who was never threatened can be robbed, while a large debtor who was threatened is safe forever. Ported faithfully; tests 'can have you robbed after a year if you haven't been threatened' and 'doesn't rob you once you've been threatened (faithful quirk)' in test/engine/lender.test.ts document it.

title: Repairs are free when you pay McHenry yourself
description: offer_repair only changes cash when Wu covers a shortfall; if you can afford the amount you enter, nothing is deducted, so every self-paid repair is free. Ported faithfully; test 'never charges you when you pay yourself (faithful quirk)' in test/engine/shipyard.test.ts documents it.

title: Partial repairs are backwards, plus repair message glitches
description: offer_repair sets remaining damage to damage * paid / cost, so paying 90% of the quote leaves 90% of the damage (should be the reverse). Also: a leftover debug message 'fixing N' is shown to the player, and the quote says 'N% damaged' using raw damage points rather than a percent (repairPercent). Ported faithfully; tests in test/engine/shipyard.test.ts document it.

title: Cannon fire can sink more pirate ships than exist
description: fire_cannons keeps firing every gun after the last ship sinks, rolling health for phantom replacements, so the pirate count can go negative and the message says 'We got N of the buggers!' instead of 'all'. Should stop firing once pirates reach 0. Ported faithfully; test 'can sink more ships than there are (faithful quirk)' in test/engine/battle.test.ts documents it.

title: Hazards start in month 12, not after it
description: check_safety returns when current_time() < 12, so police/muggers/fire can happen in month 12; SPEC and the other features use > 12. Ported faithfully; test in test/engine/safety.test.ts documents it.

title: Location-specific pricing
description: Prices shouldn't be totally random: each city should have goods that are typically cheaper or more expensive there, so routes between ports matter. Starting point: the 'based' pricing mode already ported from pypan.py (setPrices(rng, city, based=true) in src/engine/prices.ts, BASE_PRICES table in constants.ts, off via BASED_PRICES). Decide whether to tune that table/sigma or design a new per-city price profile, then switch it on. Note it clamps to 5-30x magnitude, the same range as random mode; price shocks still apply on top.

title: McHenry repair: add dialogue line and verify cost is deducted from cash
description: When you ask McHenry to fix your ship, he should say "Aye, she'll be right as rain for ye!!" Also, double-check that the price of repairs is deducted from cash.

title: Verify pirates killed is proportional to number of cannons
description: Double-check that the number of pirates you kill is proportional to the number of cannons you have.

comments.author: ed.peters
comments.text: Verified, no bug: kills per volley scale linearly with guns (~0.55/gun in year 1, ~0.4 by year 4, as pirate health grows). Added a regression test in battle.test.ts.

title: Rebalance consignments: poor income-to-hold-space ratio
description:
Consignments are frequently a waste of time - they don't provide a good income-to-hold-space ratio.

Proposed pricing: shrewd trading usually triples your money in ~5 months (~25%/month). A consignment is guaranteed one-month income with much less risk, so it should pay a smaller boost: about 15% of your money, scaled by the share of the hold it takes up (value = 15% x money x size / shipSize).

title: Visit McHenry from the Hong Kong port menu
description: When in Hong Kong, it should be possible to visit McHenry from the option menu.

title: Cloudflare deployment
description: Deploy to Cloudflare. Not started; for now just keep the build static and storage behind the SaveStore interface.

title: Chance of robbery after visiting the bank
description: After visiting the bank, there should be a chance of being robbed. Apply the same odds as when arriving at a harbor.

title: Bank representative randomly appears in other ports
description: Your banker should randomly show up in different ports. Apply the same odds as for a lorcha. Report this by saying, "Good joss!! A representative from your bank is in ((port name)) for the month. You may transact with him as normal." and then add a "Visit bank" option to the menu.

title: Buy warehouses in different ports
description: You're currently limited to storing goods in Hong Kong, with the occasional option of a lorcha. What if we could buy warehouses in other ports? Comment on the impact to gameplay and balance. (From features.txt.)

title: Price shocks should keep normal price granularity per good
description: When a price shock happens, the resulting price should have the same granularity as the normal prices - general price is a whole number, arms price is a multiple of 10, silk price is a multiple of 100, etc.

title: Sponsoring traders: lend to other traders at interest
description: What if, at a certain level of success, other traders would come to you for a loan? This would essentially turn you into your own version of Elder Brother Wu - you loan money for interest, periodically run into them and either threaten or attack them. (From features.txt.)

title: Hire better bodyguards to repel muggers and Wu's cutthroats
description: What if, as with arming your ship, you could hire better bodyguards that might repel the attack from EBW, or the random mugging? How much would they cost and where would you hire them? (From features.txt.)

title: Ship armor: trade hold space for protection from cannon fire
description: What if there was periodically the option to add armor to your ship? It would decrease hold space in return for repelling cannon fire during battles (but being destroyed in the process). (From features.txt.)

title: New ports, opened by a steamship or other advance
description: After a couple hundred rounds, the list of ports gets a little stale. What if there was a way to open up new ports - perhaps by trading in for a steamship after an advance in technology? What would that look like? (From features.txt.)

title: Streamline menu flows to cut taps
description: The game is somewhat menu-heavy. Consider where a streamlined flow would improve playability. Examples: if the player selects Sell and the ship holds only one good, just ask whether to sell all of it. If they select Transfer and both the ship and the warehouse hold the same good, ask something like "How much ((good)) do you want in your ship's hold?"

title: Engine: seedable RNG and constants
description: src/engine/rng.ts: seedable PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) plus helpers mirroring pypan.py: randint, randfloat, chanceOf(n), randrange(n), inRange(lo,hi). Must be injectable so tests can pass a scripted stub that returns chosen rolls. src/engine/constants.ts: all values from SPEC.md section 14, plus cities, goods, mult().
acceptance_criteria: Same seed gives the same sequence; helper ranges match Python semantics (unit tested); a stub RNG can force any roll.

title: Engine: Hong state model and JSON save format
description: src/engine/hong.ts: Hong as plain data plus helpers (advanceTime, currentTime, repairPercent, totalGoods, shipAvailable, warehouseUsed/Available, isOverloaded, isBroke, netWorth). Guns vs debt starting configurations. Cargo type. serialize/deserialize with the same JSON shape as pypan.json (etc/pypan.json is a sample).
acceptance_criteria: Round-trips to JSON; loads etc/pypan.json; helper tests cover capacity with guns and special cargo.

title: Engine: prompt protocol, Game driver, scripted test harness
description: src/engine/prompts.ts: Prompt union (say with optional art, yn, choose with labeled options + cancellable, number with max) and the Flow generator type. src/engine/game.ts: Game wraps a flow generator; exposes current prompt and answer(value), validates answers against the prompt. test helper play(seed|rng, answers[]) that drives a flow and records the transcript of prompts.
acceptance_criteria: A toy flow can be stepped by tests and by a UI with no DOM coupling; invalid answers are rejected without advancing; harness returns the transcript and final state.

title: Engine: trading, pricing and price shocks
description: Port set_prices (random mode; keep BASED_PRICES table behind the flag), establish_prices (price shocks after month 1, 1-in-10, factor 5-9, flavor messages), buy_goods, sell_goods, condition report. SPEC.md sections 4.1-4.3.
